threshold.value: Clopper-Pearson upper bound at n/2 for the trials kept (63.19% at n = 60, i.e. >= 38/60)
threshold.quote: CH18 §2.5: "A differentiated EEG response (i.e. a positive response), as detected by the BCI, was defined as a classification accuracy exceeding the chance threshold calculated based on a binomial distribution. We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015))."
threshold.half_stated: the stated rule is a binomial p < .05 at n = 60 after Combrisson and Jerbi: binoinv(0.95, 60, 0.5) = 36, so > 60% (37/60, one-sided p = 0.046) [derived]; a two-sided reading needs 39/60; the variant's 38/60 matches neither, and it uses the kept-trial n, not 60

cornell.quote: The EEG was recorded with 37 electrodes (Nihon Kohden collodion-pasted Ag/AgCl cup electrodes, 1.5 mm) arranged via an augmented 10-20 system with 18 additional electrodes
cornell.source: CU18 (Brain 141:1404-1421) p. 1406; GF11 §2.3: 'The EEG was recorded using 29 [...] or 37 electrodes'
cornell.our_value: 19 10-20 sites, Hjorth Laplacian over those 19 (CU18 names NOT STATED)
cornell.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate for OM1 (fewer channels give fewer chances of an uncorrected contiguous run); unknown for OM2, whose BH family shrinks with the channel count; not measured

cornell.stated_value: CU18: 'two contiguous Hz or more'; GF11: 'greater than 2 Hz'
cornell.quote: Frequency spans smaller than 2 Hz are correlated as a result of our choices of multitaper function parameters and thus, we only considered spectral differences spanning two contiguous Hz or more to be significant.
cornell.source: CU18 p. 1408; GF11 §2.8: 'present for all frequencies contiguously over a range greater than 2 Hz'
cornell.our_value: > 2 Hz (GF11) for every variant and the 130 reading
cornell.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate than under CU18's >= 2 Hz (one more 1/3-Hz bin is needed; not measured)

cornell.stated_value: 1-50 Hz band-pass after concatenating the cleaned epochs and the Laplacian
cornell.quote: The cleaned signals from each condition were concatenated separately, converted to the Hjorth Laplacian montage in order to increase ability to localize the sources of recorded signals, and band-pass filtered between 1–50 Hz
cornell.our_value: 1-50 Hz zero-phase 4th-order Butterworth on the continuous signal before the Laplacian (no splice edges)
cornell.likely_direction: unknown (CU18's order filters across splice edges, ours does not; not measured)

cornell.stated_value: GF11: rmlinesc 60-Hz regression and runica ICA
cornell.quote: To remove 60 Hz line noise, we applied a frequency-domain regression based on Thomson’s F-test, (Thomson, 1982; Percival and Walden, 1993) implemented by the code rmlinesc from the Chronux toolbox [...]. To remove muscle, eye movement and eye blink artifact, we used independent components analysis (ICA), as implemented by EEGLAB’s runica tool
cornell.source: GF11 §2.5 (PMC3162107); CU18 describes visual pruning only (catalogue §4.2)
cornell.our_value: neither applied (as CU18); epochs pruned by the variant's prune rule

mbmi.quote: Attach 16 EEG channels to the subject's head using an electrode cap. Use the positions: FC3, FCz, FC4, C5, C3, C1, Cz, C2, C4, C6, CP3, CP1, CPz, CP2, CP4, and Pz according to the extended international 10-20 system
mbmi.source: OR17 Protocol (PMC5613801); GU17 (PMC5418541): 'Data were recorded from Fz, C3, Cz, C4, CP1, CPz, CP2, Pz for the P300 paradigms, and the motor imagery paradigm used sites FC3, FC4, C5, C1, C2, C6, CP3, and CP4 as well.'
mbmi.our_value: 11 nearest 10-20 sites, duplicates dropped (FC3->F3, FC4->F4, C5->T7, C6->T8, C1->C3, C2->C4, CP1/CP3->P3, CP2/CP4->P4, CPz->Pz)
mbmi.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate for the csp = global variants (CSP on 11 channels has less room to overfit all trials); unknown for fold-wise CSP; not measured

dubois.stated_value: 16-channel g.Nautilus full set and a 9-channel motor set (Fig. 2)
dubois.quote: EEG was recorded from 16 channels (Fig. 2) with active electrodes using a g.Nautilus Wireless Research EEG headset
dubois.source: DB26 'Data acquisition'; 'Offline signal processing': 'Two EEG channel sets [16-channel full coverage; 9-channel motor cortex-focused]'
dubois.our_value: full = 17 10-20 sites (all but Fp1/Fp2); motor = F3 Fz F4 C3 Cz C4 P3 Pz P4
dubois.likely_direction: unknown (one more channel in the full set gives CSP slightly more room; not measured)

dubois.quote: The EEG was filtered (Butterworth, 0.5–100 Hz, eighth order), and sampled (sampling rate: 250 Hz, down-sampled to 125 Hz).
dubois.our_value: each recording's native rate, no resampling (BDSP 128 Hz; PDOC EDF and I-CARE files at their stored rates; engine._load)
dubois.likely_direction: negligible expected (every band is at or below 40 Hz; not measured)

dubois.stated_value: Butterworth 0.5-100 Hz, eighth order, before any analysis
dubois.quote: The EEG was filtered (Butterworth, 0.5–100 Hz, eighth order), and sampled (sampling rate: 250 Hz, down-sampled to 125 Hz).
dubois.our_value: no broadband filter: the recordings are used as stored (engine._load applies none; the staged BDSP x19 arrays are the raw channels, test_bdsp_io; the staged files carry no acquisition-filter metadata, only data, Fs and channel names); each of the six bands is filtered directly by a zero-phase 4th-order Butterworth band-pass (motor_common.bandpass, sosfiltfilt)
dubois.likely_direction: negligible expected within the analysed 1-40 Hz, which the stated pass band covers; the recordings' own acquisition filters are unknown; not measured

dubois.stated_value: delta 0.5-4, theta 4-8, mu 8-12, low beta 12-18, high beta 18-28, low gamma 28-40 Hz
dubois.quote: EEG signals were filtered into six standard frequency bands [0.5–4 Hz (delta), 4–8 Hz (theta), 8–12 Hz (mu), 12–18 Hz (low beta), 18–28 Hz (high beta), 28–40 Hz (low gamma)]
dubois.source: DB26 'Offline signal processing' (Fig. 3 legend text); catalogue §9.2 omitted it (errata)
dubois.our_value: delta 1-4, theta 4-8, mu 8-13, low beta 13-20, high beta 20-30, low gamma 30-40 Hz

dubois.quote: using Simulink FIR filters [...] (band-pass attenuation: 0 dB; band-stop: 60 dB)

dubois.stated_value: three CSP filter pairs (six filters) per band
dubois.quote: For each frequency band, three CSP filter pairs (six filters total) were retained.
dubois.our_value: 2 filters from each end per band (4 per band, 16 per band set)
dubois.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate (16 instead of 24 candidate features per band set for the 4-10-feature MI selection, so less selection on noise; not measured)

dubois.stated_value: mutual information with a fixed quantisation level of 3
dubois.quote: The MI between each feature and the class label was computed using a fixed quantisation level of 3.
dubois.source: DB26 'Feature selection (mutual information)'; catalogue §9.2 omitted it (errata)

dubois.quote: CSP-filtered signals were transformed into feature vectors using a sliding window of either 1 s or 2 s (depending on the FBCSP-MuI setup), with a 40 ms step size between windows.
dubois.our_value: DA every 100 ms; the stated 200-ms smoothing as a centred 3-point boxcar
dubois.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate for the DA > 70% arm (a coarser grid scans fewer points for the maximum); unknown for the paired t, where the task and the baseline maxima both fall; not measured

dubois.stated_value: final peak = raw-curve local maximum within ± 150 ms of the smoothed peak
dubois.quote: A final peak DA was then selected from the non-smoothed DA curve as the local maximum within a ± 150 ms (300 ms total) window centred on the smoothed peak.
dubois.source: DB26 'Peak DA extraction'; catalogue §9.2 omitted it (errata)
dubois.our_value: not implemented: the peak is the smoothed maximum (frozen reading A and 130 reading B)
dubois.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate for the DA > 70% arm (a raw maximum over the 300-ms window is at least the 200-ms smoothed value it is centred on [derived]); unknown for the paired t; not measured

dubois.stated_value: −3 s to +5 s epochs, but a 0.4-7 s task interval
dubois.quote: For each run, task-relevant EEG segments were extracted from −3 s to +5 s relative to the onset of the motor imagery cue.
dubois.source: DB26 'Epoching'; 'Time-varying decoding accuracy calculation': 'The baseline (reference) interval was defined from −1000 to 0 ms before the task cue. [...] the task interval was defined from 400 ms to 7000 ms post-cue.'
dubois.our_value: −3 s to +7 s of data (DA grid −1 to 7 s; trailing 1-2 s windows): the stated −3 s start is met; the end is +7 s against the stated +5 s, forced by the stated 0.4-7 s task interval
dubois.likely_direction: unknown (the stated values conflict; not measured)

cruse11.stated_value: 25 EGI electrodes over the motor area, each referenced to its four geodesically nearest of 129
cruse11.quote: We selected the 25 electrodes over the motor area (covering the area centrally from C3 to C4 [figure 1]) from the original 129-channel electrodes
cruse11.source: CR11 pp. 2-3; p. 2: 'We re-referenced all channels offline, including the online reference, to the average of their four geodesically nearest neighbours with a laplacian operator.'
cruse11.our_value: 9 10-20 sites F3 Fz F4 C3 Cz C4 P3 Pz P4; each minus the equal-weight mean of its 4 nearest of the 19 10-20 sites by great-circle arc (25 EGI names NOT STATED)
cruse11.likely_direction: unknown (about 10,800 instead of about 30,000 features per trial [derived: 9 or 25 x 4 bands x 300 samples]; not measured)

cruse11.stated_value: bad channels by inspection (variance > ~250) replaced by interpolation
cruse11.quote: We identified bad channels by inspection (channel variance of about >250) and replaced them with interpolations of their neighbours (InvDist, EEGLAB).

cruse11.stated_value: baseline corrected in the 500 ms before the tone
cruse11.quote: segmented into epochs of 5·5 s (including 1·5 s before every tone), and baseline corrected in 500 ms before the tone.
cruse11.likely_direction: none expected: a constant per epoch and channel does not change 7-30 Hz band power (module FIXED), edge transients of an epoch-wise band filter aside; not measured

edlow17.quote: The motor paradigm matrix had a shorter duration (76 features by 388 seconds) due to the removal of data collected during repeated instructions for that paradigm.
edlow17.source: ED17-S pp. 8-9; same paragraph: 'we excluded data collected during the first second after a repeated instruction ("keep squeezing", "keep resting") during the motor imagery paradigm.'
edlow17.our_value: 384 s: all 4 instructions per block and the following second dropped (1-s instruction assumed; a uniform per-block rule cannot give 388: 188 s / 24 blocks = 7.83 s [derived])
edlow17.likely_direction: negligible expected (4 of 388 columns; not measured)

edlow17.stated_value: ICA by a research neuropsychologist; patients' large-artefact trials discarded by consensus review
edlow17.quote: Artefact rejection was performed with EEGlab using independent component analysis by a research neuropsychologist (C.C.). For patients, trials with large artefacts were discarded by consensus review
edlow17.our_value: no ICA; a 1-s column is dropped if any channel exceeds |200| µV after 1-30 Hz filtering

cruse12p.quote: Data were re-referenced offline to form two bipolar channels (FC3-CP3, FC4-CP4) that shall be referred to as C3' and C4'.
cruse12p.our_value: F3-P3 and F4-P4 (10-20 data lack FC3/FC4/CP3/CP4; both straddle C3/C4 as the originals do)
cruse12p.likely_direction: unknown (a longer bipolar span; not measured)

errata.error: The catalogue quoted the configuration search, CV, intervals, smoothing, t-test and permutation but omitted five stated constants: the six band edges, three CSP filter pairs per band, the MI quantisation level, the 40-ms step and the ± 150-ms peak refinement (also the Simulink FIR filter type and the −3 to +5 s epoch). The frozen pipe_dubois FIXED values for these were therefore chosen as if NOT STATED ('sub-band edges NOT in the catalogue').
quotes: EEG signals were filtered into six standard frequency bands [0.5–4 Hz (delta), 4–8 Hz (theta), 8–12 Hz (mu), 12–18 Hz (low beta), 18–28 Hz (high beta), 28–40 Hz (low gamma)] using Simulink FIR filters [...] (band-pass attenuation: 0 dB; band-stop: 60 dB).
For each frequency band, three CSP filter pairs (six filters total) were retained.
The MI between each feature and the class label was computed using a fixed quantisation level of 3.
CSP-filtered signals were transformed into feature vectors using a sliding window of either 1 s or 2 s (depending on the FBCSP-MuI setup), with a 40 ms step size between windows.
A final peak DA was then selected from the non-smoothed DA curve as the local maximum within a ± 150 ms (300 ms total) window centred on the smoothed peak.
For each run, task-relevant EEG segments were extracted from −3 s to +5 s relative to the onset of the motor imagery cue.
errata.source: DB26 (PMC13272656), 'Offline signal processing', 'Epoching', 'Spatial filtering (CSP)', 'Feature extraction', 'Feature selection (mutual information)', 'Peak DA extraction'
errata.consequence: All are constant across the du Bois variants: listed under constant_departures.dubois and, per decision 1, do not affect eligibility. The catalogue file itself was not edited.

quotes: Briefly, a naïve Bayes classifier estimates the parameters of a probability distribution (in this case, the mean and standard deviation of a normal distribution) per training feature per class.
